sources.title: Mark Srednicki, Quantum Field Theory (author-hosted 2006 prepublication book draft)
sources.locator: §12, ‘Dimensional Analysis with hbar = c = 1,’ printed pp. 104–105 (PDF pp. 103–104), equations (12.1)–(12.12) and Problems 12.1–12.3.

contents.name: §12: natural-unit conversion, dimensionless action, scalar field and coupling dimensions

source_review.read_extent: The complete §12 text was read from its opening natural-unit conversions through equations (12.1)–(12.12), the high-energy discussion, and the three end-of-section problems.
source_review.supports: Natural units turn time and length into inverse-mass units; a dimensionless action fixes the density dimension and the canonical scalar-field engineering dimension.
source_review.limitations: The source uses mass powers and hbar = c = 1; this item converts them to inverse-length powers and separately derives its SI normalizations. Its perturbative and renormalizability discussion is not adopted as a QFT existence claim.

contents.name: §12 high-energy interpretation of dimensionful couplings
contents.reason: This pair fixes engineering dimensions and a finite model boundary; it does not assert perturbative control, renormalizability, high-energy behavior, or the existence of an interacting continuum theory.

source_review.read_extent: The discussion following equation (12.12) was read through the end of §12.
source_review.supports: The source relates coupling mass dimension to a perturbative high-energy parameter.
source_review.limitations: No such perturbative or ultraviolet conclusion is required by the assigned unit dictionary.

contents.name: Problems 12.1–12.3: numerical conversions and proton-radius estimate
contents.reason: These exercises request numerical particle conversions and a measured proton-radius comparison; this pair introduces no measurements, numerical estimates, or empirical data.

source_review.read_extent: All three exercises at the end of §12 were read.
source_review.supports: They identify numerical natural-unit conversions and one explicitly measured quantity as separate exercises.
source_review.limitations: The assigned statement records symbolic conversions only and reports no measurements.
